title: AI Contract Review Automation
summary: AI contract review automation allows legal teams to standardize clause evaluation and accelerate document processing times by using predefined playbooks.
body_markdown:
## Building your first contract review bot


A linear sequence is required for reliable automated screening. A no-code automation platform, such as Zapier for simplicity or Make for complex logic, orchestrates the movement of document data between your inbox and an LLM.


### Triggering contract review with new email attachments


The workflow begins by monitoring a specific intake channel, typically a shared legal inbox. In an automation builder, you select Gmail as the trigger app and "New Attachment" as the event.


To avoid processing image signatures, apply a filter for file extensions ending in ".pdf" or ".docx".


The automation platform must hand the file off to a dedicated parser like Adobe PDF Services to convert the document into a raw text string.


### Converting PDF contracts into readable text


Large Language Models are designed to process tokens, which are essentially numerical representations of text characters. A PDF file is a binary format containing complex instructions for how to render fonts and layouts on a screen, which the AI cannot read directly.


The parsing step is the bridge that translates this binary data into a clean, sequential text string that the LLM can ingest.


Even though some models are multimodal, providing a raw text string remains the most reliable way to ensure the AI analyzes every specific word of a legal clause without distraction.


### Connecting the document to the parsing engine


This hand-off requires a separate API subscription to a parsing service, which you link to your automation platform using an API key.


The platform sends the binary file content to the parser's endpoint, where the service extracts the text and returns it as a structured data object.


You then map this returned text variable into the next step of your flow, ensuring the AI receives a clean string rather than a raw file.


### Extracting contract text with open source libraries


If you prefer to avoid third-party parsing subscriptions, you can handle text extraction using built-in code steps within your automation platform.


Most platforms allow you to run a Python or Node.js script that utilizes open-source libraries like PyPDF2 or pdf-parse to read the binary data directly.


By writing a short script to loop through the document pages, you can concatenate the text into a single variable. This approach keeps your data within your own automation environment and eliminates the per-document cost of external parsing services.


### Step 2: Map your legal playbook to an AI prompt


Standardizing review criteria involves translating your firm’s "Red Flag" list into a structured system prompt. You must define specific indemnity thresholds, jurisdiction requirements, and termination notice periods.


By using a high-reasoning model like Claude Fable 5.2, the system can handle the long-horizon task of comparing a hundred-page document against these rules without losing context.


### Step 3: Extract and score clauses automatically


The core processing step sends the parsed text and your playbook to the LLM. Configure the model (such as GPT-6 Astra) to output findings in a structured format, identifying the clause number, the problematic text, and a risk score.


Activepieces connects these legal analysis steps to the team's existing tools while exposing every connected integration as a tool for the AI agent.


The same integration action that runs in a deterministic flow is exposed as an MCP tool, a mechanism visible in the` packages/pieces` directory of the open source repository.


This allows an agent to call a contract review tool directly from a chat interface without a second integration step, leveraging a library of 748 integrations where roughly 60% are community-contributed, ensuring a vast ecosystem of third-party support is available to the user, which means the platform relies heavily on external developers to maintain its breadth.


For internal compliance reviews, this structured logging in Google Sheets creates a permanent audit trail of every automated decision.


### Step 4: Route high-risk contracts for human approval


The final stage uses a conditional "Router" step. If the LLM assigns a "High" risk score, the platform triggers an immediate alert via Slack, providing a direct link to the document and the specific flags raised.


This ensures the legal team prioritizes contracts with significant liability gaps.
